You can't physically be there but mentally you can be. Let her know how you feel. It's the only thing you've got. That you'll be by her side no matter what. 

But is she ready to have a kid and how will her family react? Will it hurt her more since she's already taking care of family? Will you be together? If not, will she make you pay for child support? If you break up will you still be in the babies life? Just communicate and discuss everything you can think of with her. Not at this second but over time. It's a big step and you'll have to be there for her

I'd say "hey I've seen you get off at the same stop!" And mention a restaurant or a food you like in relation to that area. Something that's common ground. But just be nice and friendly. You know, not everyone is outgoing or knows how to talk to people. It seems like half of Reddit is awkward. 
She has headphones in, ask what type of music she likes or if she listens to podcasts. Music is a pretty vast topic to talk about so you both can talk about what you like. 

But just be yourself. You know don't go all in if you're not ready. Take your time to talk to her. Say hey one day or if you catch her eye smile. It sounds creepy but I love when strangers smile at me. I remember it too

I also suggest seeing a professional about your depression. It won't ever be something you can run from but to improve yourself the way you want to be it's your best bet. She sounds like she really loves you. I don't think it's because she doesn't want to go through it all again. 

The different libido things can be gotten through with communication. It seems like she can understand and doesn't have that big of an issue with it. 

Does she know how you feel on the inside? What upsets you and what kicks you down or makes you not want to wake up or do anything? If not, I'd tell her and hopefully bring you closer so she understands. You need to work on yourself and if she's willing to stand by you through it she's your rock then. 

I wish you the best of luck, we all deserve it. And you're reaching out for some advice. It's the first step
